intro: This 6 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 review brings together unofficial candidate reports. The shift cards show section difficulty and recalled topics from the remaining sources. Some reviews have limited evidence and need further corroboration. Exam-wide survey averages are excluded from shift-specific good-attempt estimates; an unavailable total means no reliable recommendation is being made. SSC publishes the official answer key and applies its own score normalisation.

shifts.summary: Candidates reported overall difficulty ranging from Easy to Difficult, with most labeling it Moderate. Good attempts varied between 70 and 92 out of 100. Reasoning was generally easy, while Quant had mixed difficulty and English was mostly easy. Time pressure from sectional timers and lengthy questions was a common issue.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: A few long questions caused time pressure; some puzzle and number‑series questions were skipped. Slog questions were lengthy and tricky. Coding‑decoding and analogy items were present but not overly hard.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Questions were factual; options often needed deeper knowledge. Current affairs focused on one‑liners and older events. GK difficulty ranged from easy to moderate.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Time shortage on lengthy calculations; many advanced arithmetic and mensuration items. Some sections had heavy advanced math weightage causing pressure.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Reading comprehension passages were easy to moderate. Spelling and idiom questions added some difficulty.

faqs.q: What difficulty was reported on 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1: Moderate (reports differ); Shift 2: Easy to Moderate (reports differ); Shift 3: Easy to Difficult (reports differ). These are unofficial candidate-review summaries.

faqs.q: Is the analysis for 6 October 2026 complete and official?
faqs.a: Read the individual shift pages for source coverage, recalled topics and correction notes. The analysis is not an official paper or SSC statement.

faqs.q: Why are some good-attempt figures unavailable for 6 October 2026?
faqs.a: A pooled survey average, accuracy percentage or conflicting total does not establish how many questions were safe to attempt in a particular shift. Those figures are withheld rather than replaced with guesses.
